title: A debug build fails an index assert in `dp_matrix.rs` on the fixtures
body:
With debug assertions on, which means any build but release, this command fails on `dev` at `837ba60`:

```bash
nail search fixtures/query.hmm fixtures/target.fa --seeds fixtures/a.seeds --mmseqs-path /bin/true -t 1
```

The assert `profile_idx <= self.profile_length` at `libnail/src/align/structs/dp_matrix.rs:831` fails. libnail's `backward.rs` reaches it, called from `nail/src/pipeline/align_stage.rs:151`. A release build skips the assert, runs to completion and writes 408 hits. Every seed in `a.seeds` has its `prf_end` within its profile's `LENG`, so the seeds file is not the cause.

## Open

- Either the assert is wrong or `backward` indexes past the profile length.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text:
Diagnosis at `eeab798`. The issue's command no longer reaches the assert: `fixtures/a.seeds` names its records, and `--seeds` reads positions since `dbdee02` (nail-a32cbf). With the same 410 seeds converted to positions, a debug build fails the same assert, `profile_idx <= self.profile_length` in `DpMatrixSparse::match_idx` (`dp_matrix.rs:831`), called from `backward`.

The read comes from the inner loop of the main recursion in `backward.rs`, `for profile_idx in (profile_start_on_current_row..=profile_end_on_current_row).rev()`. On a row whose right bound is the profile length L, the iteration at L reads `get_match(target_idx + 1, L + 1)` and `get_delete(target_idx, L + 1)`, one position past the model.

The read does not change any result:

- Every term that uses a cell at L + 1 also adds a score that is minus infinity at that position. The match term adds `match_score(residue, L + 1)` and the delete term adds the MD or DD transition at L. On all four `fixtures/query.hmm` profiles these are minus infinity: match score at L + 1 for every residue, MD and DD at L, and insert score at L. So each log-sum term that touches L + 1 is minus infinity whatever the cell holds, and the cell at L comes out as E, the value set just before the loop.
- `DpMatrixSparse::reuse` lays out each row as [left - 1, right], a pad cell then the row, and `match_idx` clamps with `.min(next_block_offset)`. A read at right + 1 therefore lands on the next row's pad cell, which is reset to minus infinity and never written. The comment above that `min` says it exists to keep reads from moving right out of a block.

So `backward` is correct and the assert is stricter than the layout it guards: the layout supports reads up to right + 1, which is L + 1 on a full-width row. Release builds skip the assert and get the same values.

## Ways to fix it, not chosen

- Relax the assert to `profile_idx <= self.profile_length + 1`, which states what the layout supports.
- Keep the assert and stop `backward` from reading L + 1, for example by starting the loop below the end cell when the right bound is L. The cell at L is already set to E before the loop.
